decisions.reason: The necessary cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, which restores the approved Hero V as the fixed geometry and requires the accent and surrounding type to adapt to it.
The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY requiring the E and L forms, as surrounding type, to adapt to the approved Hero V without changing its geometry.
The existing state already requires the shared terminal gesture to derive from the approved Hero V; fixing the Hero V as the alignment reference does not alter that terminal-treatment requirement.
The candidate already requires the É accent to be the literal terminal section of the approved Hero V with an exact vector match, so the source clarification introduces no additional state change.
Restoring the Hero V and making surrounding type adapt to it does not change the established second-V hierarchy of sitting above the E and L while remaining below the Hero V and É accent.
The second V is already required to derive its geometry and signature gesture from the approved Hero V; the source decision does not establish a different second-V geometry rule.
The source decision concerns geometry reference and peak alignment, not spacing or the requirement that the wordmark read as one unified mark.
The source decision does not change the deferred champagne material treatment or its role relative to the resolved geometry.
The Hero V alignment-reference clarification has no effect on the task-local obligation to include design rationale with review rounds.
